correctness.rationale: For M≥1 condition on all but one numerator Gaussian; the conditional density is strictly decreasing for z>0 and finite there, so its expectation is strictly decreasing (symmetric for z<0). For M=0, let u=−log(s_N z): multiplying the sum-of-log|G| density by e^u exactly changes the one-factor law to h(u)=exp(2u−e^(2u)/2), the strictly log-concave log-Rayleigh density; its N-fold convolution has exactly one mode and vanishes at both tails, giving precisely ±z_N and zero density at the origin. The gamma Mellin transform yields μ=(log2−γ)/2, variance π²/24 and third cumulant −ζ(3)/4; uniform Fourier differentiated local expansion then gives u_N=Nμ+3ζ(3)/π²+O(1/N). The strong law for log|G| establishes the typical growth. Independent numerical inverse-Fourier derivatives at N=1,2,5,10,50,100 corroborated mode roots and direction, while the infinite claim rests on log-concavity and the Fourier remainder proof.
residual_risks: The full asymptotic relies on Fourier remainder and uniform derivative expansion, not the finite mode checks.
